_format: Each rule: task + at least one of  op/pattern (some file of that op fullmatches),  all_of [{op,pattern},..] (every entry matches),  none_of [..] (no entry matches),  program (fullmatch on the timer program name).  Rules are tried in order; first match wins; _comment/_format keys are ignored.

_comment: Write rules first: outputs identify a task; inputs are often shared (mutation_overlap and frequency read the same files).
sifting's python process: writes sifted.SIFT.chrN.txt (the write rule alone would do); all_of shown as an example of a read-set condition.
sifting's grep child reads the annotation VCF and writes nothing the monitor sees; identified by program name. Change task to sifting_grep to keep it separate (the JSON run labels it sifting).
Fallbacks for any other read-only reader of the annotation VCF or of the grep output (one pattern per rule keeps the Sankey group labels readable).
Not a task rule: read-only pattern so the individuals input gets a readable Sankey label; never matches a process by itself because individuals always writes first.
